title: Deployment Rhythm Lab Notebook — Cutover Simulations & Summary
body:
Purpose:
Quick lab notebook for the Sept cutover simulation runs we did on 2026-09-11 and the follow-up small-scale run on 2026-09-14. Goal: validate staggered-region rollout cadence and autoscaler behavior under bursty prefix-cache churn, measure tail latency impact, and confirm rollback ergonomics.

Scope / what this is not:
- Focused on serving/runtime interactions, not infra provisioning or infra-as-code validation.
- Not a formal runbook; outputs below will be folded into the official playbook if validated.

Simulation setup (summary):
- Baseline model: gptx-13b-quant (variant q4_0) hosted on Dedicated pool (eu-west-1 primary, us-west-2 secondary).
- Traffic generator: local k6 script (scripts/cutover-bursts/k6-staggered.js) — 1000 concurrent virtual users, ramp 0->1000 over 2m, burst windows at +4m and +12m for 60s each.
- KV cache priming: 30k unique prefixes; then random 30% cache invalidation mid-run to simulate model change / cache priming effect.
- Autoscaler: target_util=0.65, scale_step=+2 nodes, cooldown=90s.
- Observability hooks: token latency histogram, tail-99.9, per-instance CPU/GPU utilization, request queue length (runtime queue), and request-fanout metrics.
- Failure injection: simulated pod termination (SIGTERM) on 1/8 nodes at t=+8m in one run.

Key timeline (staggered rollout cadence we wanted to exercise):
- t0 (00:00) — canary lane (1% traffic) flips to new runtime flag A.
- t+10m — ramp to 10% in eu-west-1 only.
- t+30m — roll to 30% with autoscaler warm-up.
- t+60m — full region switchover to 100% in eu-west-1, begin us-west-2 slow ramp.
- fallback policy: if tail-99.9 > 800ms for > 5m OR error-rate > 0.8% for > 10m, auto-fallback to previous model variant and trigger alert.

Preflight checklist (what we actually validated before runs):
- [x] Smoke tests green (runtime smoke job 2026-09-10).
- [x] Canary infra snapshot saved (gz archive in s3://redwood-release-snapshots/2026-09-11-canary.tgz).
- [x] Observability dashboards pinned + alert thresholds staged.
- [x] Slack #release-alerts subscription checked — escalation list confirmed.
- [ ] Ops pager rota (need confirmation from SRE on weekend cover) — TODO: Aisha to confirm.

During-cutover play snippets (notes + sticky ops actions):
- At first burst (t+4m) we saw queue length jump 3x but latency remained within 400ms p99.
- After cache invalidation event, cold-KV miss amplified GPU memory copies causing p99.9 spikes ~1.2s for ~150s window.
- Autoscaler triggered scale_step twice; node spin-up latency ~75s average, but steady-state node readiness delayed by warm GPU kernel caches (~40s).
- Pod termination injection at t+8m produced transient 503s in 0.04% of requests; rollback path exercised and successful.

Immediate issues observed (actionable):
1) GPU kernel warmup time contributes materially to end-to-end tail latency. Consider pre-warming kernels during node boot (early-init hook) — owner: Ravi.
2) Autoscaler aggressive step creates oscillation when combined with prefix-churn. Add hysteresis to scale_down path — owner: SRE squad (cc: Sofia).
3) Alert threshold for tail-99.9 currently set to 500ms which caused a false-positive during controlled cache churn. Increase to 800ms for staged ramp windows, but keep 500ms for steady-state.

Quantified results (summary table):
- Run A (2026-09-11 baseline ramp):
  - avg latency (token roundtrip): 95ms
  - p99: 320ms
  - p99.9: 780ms (spike windows)
  - error rate: 0.07%
  - autoscaler node adds: 4 total; avg spin-up 75s

- Run B (2026-09-14 modified autoscaler/hysteresis):
  - avg latency: 110ms (slightly higher due to conservative batching configuration)
  - p99: 290ms
  - p99.9: 610ms
  - error rate: 0.03%
  - autoscaler node adds: 2 total; avg spin-up 72s

Interpretation / tradeoffs:
- Hysteresis reduces oscillation and lowers error rate and extreme tail, but increases average latency slightly because we opted for a safer batching window. This trade is acceptable for customer-facing SLAs.
- Kernel warmup remains primary contributor to transient 503s when pod churn aligns with cache invalidation. Need engineering work to precompile/common-cache patterns.

Rollback matrix (quick reference):
- Trigger conditions: tail-99.9 > 800ms for > 5 min OR error-rate > 0.8% for > 10 min OR sustained 5xx > 0.5% for > 2 min.
- Steps:
  1) Announce in #release-alerts, mark as rollback in release tracker.
  2) Flip traffic routing to previous model variant (route -> variant:v_prev) via control-plane API (POST /route/switch).
  3) Gradual drain new runtime nodes (conn-drain=60s) while re-adding previous nodes.
  4) Run smoke tests; if green, cutover complete, file follow-up ticket for root cause.

Post-run artifacts to produce (next 72h):
- Formal playbook entry with the updated hysteresis settings and alert thresholds (owner: me).
- Follow-up PR to runtime repo to add early-init kernel pre-warm hook (PR template started: /runtime/pull/8342) — owner: Ravi.
- Postmortem-lite doc if we see repeated 5xx in production — decide by 2026-09-18.

Meeting notes (sync 2026-09-15):
- Attendees: Jordan, Aisha, Ravi, Sofia, Tom (SRE).
- Decisions: bump staged alert p99.9 threshold to 800ms during rollout windows; keep 500ms otherwise. Add autoscaler backoff of 60s after a scale event.
- Open items: confirm weekend pager (Aisha), schedule kernel pre-warm spike test (Ravi), and run a multi-region long-tail test (Jordan + SRE).

Draft release notes (to be copied into release bundle if we promote):
- runtime: improve autoscaler stability during prefix-cache churn. New default release includes conservative scale hysteresis to reduce oscillations and reduce visible 5xx spikes during rollouts.
- runtime: add telemetry markers to surface kernel warmup windows to dashboards (helpful for diagnostics).
- ops: updated rollback thresholds and automated fallback policy to reduce customer impact during high churn rollouts.

Notes to self / freeform brain dump:
- If kernel pre-warm isn't feasible at node init, consider a tiny fleet of warm standby instances that keep KV cache and kernel states sunny. Cost tradeoff vs p99.9 risk.
- Could we patch the control-plane so that the first N requests to new nodes are routed through a warming proxy that feeds kernel warmup calls rather than real traffic? Might reduce customer-visible spikes.

Relevant tickets / PRs referenced:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342 (early-init prewarm draft)
- Jira: INFR-1297 (autoscaler hysteresis proposal)
- Confluence: deployment-rhythm-lab (internal draft with raw dashboards)

Action items (owner + due):
- Aisha: confirm weekend pager rota (due 2026-09-16).
- Ravi: open PR with kernel pre-warm prototype and run unit bench (due 2026-09-20).
- Sofia: coordinate with SRE on autoscaler backoff changes and staging rollout (due 2026-09-18).
- Jordan (me): merge lab notes into release playbook and schedule multi-region long-tail test (due 2026-09-19).

End notebook. Keep this as the working lab doc; will extract official checklists into release-engineering/runbooks after the above follow-ups land.
